# intervals.library: Contains

**Status:** Supported (tier `foundation`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> True when `p` lies within the closed box \[Min, Max\] on every axis (inclusive).

### Law_ContainsStart

[stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato, line 55](../../../../../stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato#L55)

```plato
// A forward interval contains its own Start endpoint (closed interval, inclusive).
Law_ContainsStart(self: IInterval<$T>): Boolean
    => self.IsReversed || self.Contains(self.Start);
```

### Law_ContainsCenter

[stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato, line 79](../../../../../stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato#L79)

```plato
// Same property, stated over AngleInterval's OWN surface.
//
// DOMAIN: AngleInterval reinterprets both Contains and Center as ARC operations
// (intervals.library.plato), so the generic law above does
// not describe this type. Worse, monomorphizing it produces a CHIMERA: the
// interface's linear Center is inlined into the law body (resolution happens
// against IInterval, where the specialization is invisible), while the
// Contains call survives as a call and is re-bound by C# extension-method
// overload resolution to the type's wrap-aware one (tracked as plato-374). Arc
// Contains of a linear midpoint holds for neither reading, and it fails for
// every interval whose stored End - Start exceeds a turn. Restated here on the
// arc surface, where
// the midpoint is Start + Span/2 and containment always holds.
Law_ContainsCenter(self: AngleInterval): Boolean
    => self.Contains(self.Center);
```

### Line 88

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato, line 88](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato#L88).

```plato

    // True when `p` lies within the closed box [Min, Max] on every axis (inclusive).
    Contains(self: Bounds2D, p: Point2D): Boolean
        => self.Min.X <= p.X && p.X <= self.Max.X
        && self.Min.Y <= p.Y && p.Y <= self.Max.Y;
```

### Line 93

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato, line 93](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato#L93).

```plato

    // True when `other` lies entirely within this box (both its corners inside).
    Contains(self: Bounds2D, other: Bounds2D): Boolean
        => self.Contains(other.Min) && self.Contains(other.Max);
```

    // True when `p` lies within the closed box [Min, Max] on every axis (inclusive).
    Contains(self: Bounds3D, p: Point3D): Boolean
        => self.Min.X <= p.X && p.X <= self.Max.X
        && self.Min.Y <= p.Y && p.Y <= self.Max.Y
        && self.Min.Z <= p.Z && p.Z <= self.Max.Z;

### Line 221

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato, line 221](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato#L221).

```plato

    // True when `value` lies within the closed interval [Start, End] (both
    // endpoints inclusive). Assumes forward orientation; Reverse a reversed span.
    Contains(self: IInterval<$T>, value: $T): Boolean
        => self.Start <= value && value <= self.End;
```

### Line 358

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato, line 358](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/intervals.library.plato#L358).

```plato

    // True when `a` lies on the CCW arc from Start to End, endpoints inclusive and
    // seam-crossing handled: `a`'s CCW offset from Start (reduced to [0, one turn))
    // must not exceed the arc's Span. Correct across the +/-pi seam, where the linear
    // IInterval.Contains is not.
    Contains(self: AngleInterval, a: Angle): Boolean
        => (a - self.Start).Wrap(1.0.Turns) <= (self.End - self.Start).Wrap(1.0.Turns);
```
